record.original_question: Determine the thickness t(K_{r,s}) of every complete bipartite graph K_{r,s}, where thickness is the minimum number of planar subgraphs whose union contains all edges.

evidence.quote: Problem 7.1 Find the thickness of Kr,s for all r, s.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
The thickness t(G) of a finite simple graph G is defined as the minimum number of planar subgraphs of G whose union (as edge sets) equals the edge set of G. For positive integers r and s, let K_{r,s} denote the complete bipartite graph with parts of sizes r and s, having rs edges joining every pair of vertices in different parts.

Determine t(K_{r,s}) for every pair of positive integers (r,s). In particular, decide whether the formula
   t(K_{r,s}) = ⌈ rs / (2(r+s−2)) ⌉
holds for all r,s ≥ 2, and resolve the cases where r and s are both odd that are not covered by the known constructions.
artifact.status_search_result: The thickness of K_{r,s} was determined by Beineke, Harary and Moon (1964) for all cases where at least one of r,s is even, and the conjectured formula ⌈rs/(2(r+s−2))⌉ is believed to hold in general. However, infinitely many cases with both r and s odd remain open; the smallest unresolved case is reported to be K_{17,21}. Recent works have settled additional families but a complete determination is still open.

status_evidence.title: On the thickness of the complete bipartite graph
status_evidence.snippet: Beineke, Harary, Moon determined the thickness of K_{m,n} for most values of m,n.
status_evidence.claim: Thickness of K_{r,s} solved for most (r,s) but not all.

status_evidence.title: The Thickness of Some Complete Bipartite and Tripartite Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: For complete bipartite graphs, the problem has not been entirely solved yet; smallest unknown case K_{17,21}.
status_evidence.claim: Remaining odd-odd cases are still open.

status_evidence.title: Graph Thickness — Wolfram MathWorld
status_evidence.snippet: Conjectured formula ⌈mn/(2(m+n-2))⌉ for thickness of K_{m,n}.
